newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says Rwanda breaks border truce.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says Rwanda breaks border truce.

text.p: Zaire accused Rwanda on Thursday of breaking a truce negotiated after Zairean and Rwandan troops traded mortar fire across their border at the start of the week.

The deputy governor of South Kivu, Lwabandji Lwasi, told Reuters by telephone from the border town of Bukavu that shots had been fired from the Rwandan side of the border on Wednesday on the road from Bukavu to Uvira.

Zaire, host to over a million Rwandan Hutu refugees, has accused Rwanda of sending Tutsi infiltrators to destabilise its eastern refugee zone. It says they are from the Banyamulenge ethnic group, some of whom have lived in the Uvira region for generations.

"The Rwandans have violated the ceasefire that we concluded with them on Tuesday," Lwabandji said. "They fired on the road... which links Bukavu to Uvira. There were no victims (but) the people are still afraid, particularly after what happened yesterday," he added.

Lwabandji said that a group of U.S. diplomats had been forced to turn back because of the firing. No diplomats were immediately available for comment and there was no independent confirmation of the report.
The Hutu refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals after Hutu hardliners killed up to one million minority Tutsis and allied Hutus and Tutsi rebels seized power.

Relations between Zaire and Rwanda have since deteriorated, with each side accusing the other of sponsoring or failing to stop raids into their territory. Some families in Bukavu moved their children to outlying villages following mortar exchanges on Sunday and Monday nights. One Zairean died in the exchange.
